newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANY SCORE CRUCIAL 2-0 WIN OVER UKRAINE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY SCORE CRUCIAL 2-0 WIN OVER UKRAINE.

text.p: Oliver Bierhoff scored a vital goal midway through the second half to set up Germany for a badly-needed 2-0 win over leaders Ukraine in a World Cup group nine qualifier on Wednesday.
Bierhoff, who scored Germany's "golden" goal in the Euro '96 final, came good again with a powerful left foot shot in the 63rd minute to crack the stubborn Ukraine defence.
"The goal was enormously important," Bierhoff said. "It was a liberation for us. We knew they would be standing back there on defence. They played very well."
The win took Germany into second place on 11 points, one behind Ukraine and two clear of Portugal. Germany also have a match in hand.

Mario Basler broke free to score Germany's second goal in the 72nd minute, collecting a pass from Juergen Klinsmann on the left-hand side of the penalty box and looping the ball over goalkeeper Olexander Kosovsky.
Klinsmann had also set up Bierhoff's strike with a well-placed header.
"This win was very important," said German coach Berti Vogts, who had called the match the team's most crucial test this year.
Germany had managed just two wins over lowly Albania and Armenia in four qualifiers before Wednesday's match. They had been held to draws against Northern Ireland and Portugal.

"It was a very, very difficult match," Vogts added. "We managed to find our game in the second half. We wanted to put the pressure on them, but were not able to. They have very good players. We didn't play aggressively enough."
